claims.text: In CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloys, hardness and strength are governed by grain size.
CoCrFeMnNi exhibits a Hall–Petch regime in which grain refinement increases hardness and strength.
The strengthening in the Hall–Petch regime arises from dislocation pile-up and grain-boundary strengthening.
Below a critical grain size, CoCrFeMnNi enters an inverse Hall–Petch regime.
Extreme grain refinement induces dynamic amorphization, particularly in near-surface regions.
Dynamic amorphization promotes shear localization in ultrafine regions.
Amorphization-associated shear localization prevents further strengthening and produces a hardness plateau or mild hardness reduction.
Powder bed fusion under inert conditions can provide an initially coarse-grained CoCrFeMnNi state.
High-pressure torsion following additive manufacturing can generate a series spanning coarse-grained, ultrafine-grained, and nanocrystalline CoCrFeMnNi states.
XRD and DSC can identify and quantify the proposed amorphous phase content.
Samples refined to the critical grain size will have greater hardness than the coarse-grained baseline.
Samples refined to the critical grain size will have greater yield strength than the coarse-grained baseline.
Further refinement beyond the critical grain size will produce a hardness plateau or mild reduction.
The post-threshold hardness plateau or reduction will coincide with STEM and XRD/DSC indications of dynamic amorphous domains.
The coarse-grained baseline has minimal amorphous content.
The proposed behavior is limited to CoCrFeMnNi processed under inert atmospheres by additive manufacturing followed by high-pressure torsion.
Alternative phase transformations or substantial processing changes may prevent the proposed behavior.
